content: # Intercom developer FAQs Answers to frequently asked questions related to our developer documentation, APIs, webhooks, and apps. Use this article to set up your Intercom developer environment, configure a custom Help Center domain with SSL, authenticate your app via access tokens or OAuth, and manage contacts, conversations, and tickets via the Intercom API (Application Programming Interface). It also covers webhooks, pagination, building Messenger and Inbox apps, and troubleshooting common API and SSL errors. Intended for developers building integrations with Intercom. # Setting up Intercom ## How do I create a developer account? You can[ create a new developer workspace](https://app.intercom.com/a/developer-signup) for developing apps. Developer workspaces are free and intended for development purposes only. Once you've created the new workspace you can[ follow this guide](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/getting-started/) to create an app and make your first API call. ## How do I set up a custom help center domain? When you turn on your Articles Help Center, your content is available through intercom.help by default. Your URL will look like this: intercom.help/exampleapp. If you'd like to use a different URL, you can create one by manually setting up a custom domain. This will involve entering the custom domain in your Help Center settings, creating a custom CNAME record, and optionally configuring SSL. Find the full instructions for set up in our [developer documentation](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/help-center/custom-domains/). If your Help Center shows a "not found" error after setting up a custom domain, verify your CNAME record to ensure your subdomain points to the correct Intercom host: • For HTTPS Quick Setup: us.intercomhelpcenter.com (US region) • For Manual/HTTP Setup: custom.intercom.help (US region) Also check that the security protocol selected in your Help Center settings matches your DNS setup. ### How do I set up SSL? SSL (or TLS), is the most widely used way to secure the connection between your server and your browser. It ensures the connection between the server and browser is encrypted and safe, and appears as HTTPS. There are two ways to set up SSL with Articles on your custom domain: - Use a flexible SSL (using a third party DNS provider like CloudFlare or AWS CloudFront) - Use your own SSL certificate (using a TLS Termination Proxy) ### Does Intercom handle SSL certificates for custom domains? Yes! If you enable “HTTPS (quick setup)” in your Help Center settings, Intercom will automatically provision and manage an SSL certificate for your custom domain (like [https://help.ourdomain.com](https://help.ourdomain.com)). There's no need for a manual SSL setup — just point your CNAME to us.intercomhelpcenter.com, and we’ll handle the rest. **Note**: HTTPS (quick setup) isn't available by default for all workspaces - it's a setting our Support team can enable for you. Once enabled, the HTTPS (quick setup) option will appear in your Help Center settings. Follow the DNS setup instructions below to complete your configuration. ### How to enable HTTPS (quick setup) for your custom domain If you aim to switch your custom domain to HTTPS: 1. Navigate to **Settings > Help Center > Configure & Style**. 2. Head to the **Domain** section. 3. Select **HTTPS (quick setup)** as your security protocol and save the changes. You can configure SSL for your custom domain to keep sensitive information encrypted. If you want to do this, make sure you’ve set up your CNAME with a DNS provider that supports SSL, like Cloudflare. ### Advanced troubleshooting If the standard SSL and HTTPS configuration steps haven't resolved your issue, the following scenarios cover common edge cases for custom Help Center domains: - **Domain Displays as "Not Secure":** To secure your help center hosted on HTTP, consider: - Using a third-party DNS provider, such as Cloudflare or AWS CloudFront, for flexible SSL proxying. - Employing a TLS Termination Proxy for advanced SSL certificate management. ### Common HTTPS/SSL issues and troubleshooting **1. Domain Not Secure** - Ensure only Intercom's SSL certificate is active for your domain. Remove or disable any additional certificates from your host or CDN (Content Delivery Network). - If using a CDN such as Cloudflare, set the proxy status to "DNS only" (grey cloud icon). - Verify your DNS CNAME record points to the correct Intercom endpoint (us.intercomhelpcenter.com for US, eu.intercomhelpcenter.com for EU). **ERR_SSL_VERSION_OR_CIPHER_MISMATCH Error** - Confirm that no conflicting DNS (Domain Name System) records exist. Only one CNAME should be active for the domain entry. Delete any duplicates. - Ensure DNS propagation, which can take up to 72 hours, has been completed. You can use tools like [whatsmydns.net](https://www.whatsmydns.net/) to check global propagation. **2. HTTPS Setup Stuck on Pending** - Check for common DNS configuration issues, such as formatting errors in the CNAME record (for example, accidentally appending `.yourdomain.com`) or using an incorrect record type (for example, an A record instead of CNAME). - Ensure the CNAME record points to `us.intercomhelpcenter.com` (or `eu.intercomhelpcenter.com` for EU regions). - After corrections, wait for DNS propagation, which can take up to 72 hours. Use [whatsmydns.net](https://www.whatsmydns.net/) to verify global propagation before testing again. **3. HTTPS (Quick Setup) Option Not Available** - Contact Fin Support to have HTTPS quick setup enabled for your workspace — it isn't available by default. - Ensure your domain is not already in use by another Intercom account. - Verify that a CNAME record has been added to your DNS provider, pointing to `us.intercomhelpcenter.com`. **4. Access Denied Error** - Verify the CNAME record points correctly to `us.intercomhelpcenter.com`. - If using Cloudflare, set SSL to 'Flexible' or 'Full' — avoid 'Full (Strict)'. - Toggle the SSL configuration off and back on to restart the SSL provisioning sequence. # Help Center URL and domain management ## Broken URLs after migration If a migrated article URL no longer works after moving content to Intercom: - Create a new public article to replace the broken URL. - Update any calls to action or links in your content to point to the new article's URL. ## "Not found" error when articles look fine internally If your Help Center shows a "Not found" error on the public URL but articles appear correctly in your workspace: - Check whether your Help Center is set to Live in your settings. - Navigate to Settings > Help Center and set the status to Live to make the public URL accessible. # The Intercom API ## What is the current version of the API? If you are using the Intercom API, you can also change the version within the HTTP header of your request. **Note:** The developer documentation also keeps reference pages for the legacy 1.x API (URLs containing `/docs/references/1.0/` or `/docs/references/1.1/`). Those pages describe endpoints such as `/users` and `/leads` that aren't used in version 2.x. Make sure you're following the current version's reference pages under `/docs/references/rest-api/`. ## What endpoints are available in the current version of the API? Key endpoints available in version 2.18 of the Intercom API include the ones below. Newer APIs, such as Folders, Dynamic Content, Roles, Auth Tokens, and Granted Companies, are also available in 2.18. For the full list, see the [API reference](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/introduction/). ## Can I trigger an article to open in the Messenger from a button? Yes, if you'd like to trigger an article in the Messenger, you can use the `showArticle` [method](https://developers.intercom.com/installing-intercom/web/methods/#intercomshowarticle-articleid) from the JavaScript API. The article will open within the Messenger and clicking the Messenger back button will return to the previous context. If the Messenger is closed when the method is called, it will be opened first and then the article will be shown. This is available across all platforms in the Messenger. ### How to trigger an article from HTML ``` # You can add a link anywhere on your site to open an article in the Messenger: Open article ``` # Contacts ## Should I use the /users or /contacts endpoint? Use `/contacts`. In the current API, users and leads are both contacts, and you create or update them with the [Create a contact](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/contacts/createcontact) (`POST /contacts`) and [Update a contact](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/contacts/updatecontact) (`PUT /contacts/{id}`) endpoints. `POST /users` is a legacy 1.x endpoint and won't work with current API versions. ## How do I create a contact without an email address? A contact needs at least an email or an `external_id`. To create a user without an email, send your own unique identifier for them as `external_id`. In the `/contacts` endpoints this field is called `external_id`, not `user_id`. Sending `user_id` without an email returns the error `either_email_or_user_id_present validation failed`. ``` POST https://api.intercom.io/contacts { "external_id": "cust_001", "name": "Jane Doe", "custom_attributes": { "Currency": "EUR" } } ``` Any custom attributes you set must already exist in **Settings > Data > People**, otherwise the request returns an error saying the attribute doesn't exist. ## Can I bulk create users using the API? ## Bulk operations and their limitations The following bulk operations are **not** available via the API and must be handled through looped single-item requests or manual export/import: - Bulk note deletion (notes must be deleted one at a time from the workspace UI) ## How can I retrieve an archived user's data? To retrieve an archived contact's data you first need to unarchive the contact, which you can do with the [unarchive contact API endpoint](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Contacts/UnarchiveContact/) if you have the contact's ID. It's not possible to unarchive a user or contact from the UI, it has to be done through the API. ### Can I delete notes on my contacts via the API? No, there is currently no way to delete individual notes or bulk delete notes from contacts via the API. If this functionality is important for your operations, please visit the [Product Wishlist](https://community.intercom.com/ideas) to create, comment on, or upvote a feature request. Notes can be deleted manually within the workspace, but only one at a time. # Conversations ## How do I assign conversations to a team using the API? If you would like to assign a conversation to a team using the API you have two options. The first option is to assign a conversation directly to an admin or a team using the[ manage a conversation API endpoint](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Conversations/manageConversation/). You need to have access to the Intercom provisioned id for the conversation as well as the admin_id and the assignee_id. ## How do I add notes to conversations via the API? A note in an internal comment only visible to teammates. To add a note to a conversation you can use the[ reply to a conversation API endpoint](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Conversations/replyConversation/). You will need to choose a messsage_type of note and a type of "admin" along with the admin_id that the note should come from. ## How do I add tags to conversations via the API? ## How do I create a conversation using the API? You can create a conversation from the API that has been initiated by a contact (ie. user or lead) by using the[ create a conversation API endpoint](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Conversations/createConversation/). The conversation can be an in-app message only. You will also need the Intercom provisioned id for the contact and the body text to use as the message body when making the request. By default, a conversation created this way won't appear in the Inbox — and won't be searchable via Conversation search — until the contact replies to it. To make the conversation appear in the Inbox immediately, without waiting for the contact to reply, include "create_conversation_without_contact_reply": true in the request payload. This defaults to false if not provided. ## What if the conversation doesn't appear at all, even with an ID? If the request payload's body field is missing, empty, or malformed, the API can still return a success response and create a conversation shell with no message content attached. Because the Inbox can't render a conversation with no messages, opening it in the UI returns a 404 ("Could not load conversation"), even though the conversation can still be retrieved via the API by ID. If this happens, check that the integration's body field is present and non-empty, and that message_type is set correctly (e.g. inapp or email). An existing broken conversation of this kind can't be recovered — it must be recreated with a corrected payload. ## How do I delete conversations with the API? To close a conversation using the API you can use the[ manage a conversation API endpoint](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Conversations/manageConversation/). You will need to have the Intercom provisioned id of the conversation, your admin_id and use a message_type of "close". ## How can I set up custom notifications for when a teammate is assigned to a conversation? To set up a custom notification when an action is taken, such as a teammate being assigned to a conversation, you can use [webhooks](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/webhooks/). You can then subscribe to this webhook topic in the developer hub by[ following the steps in this guide](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/webhooks/setting-up-webhooks/#subscribe-to-a-webhook-topic). You'll also need to have a publicly accessible endpoint URL available for the action to take once the webhook is hit to deliver the notification to your channel of choice. ## How do I access side conversations via the API? Side conversations don't have their own dedicated endpoint, so you can’t retrieve them directly. However, when you retrieve a conversation that the side conversation is attached to, you will see conversation parts that show as `"part_type": "side_conversation_reply"` with the content of the user's messages in the side conversation. # Tickets ## How do I create a ticket using the API? To create a ticket using the Intercom API, you will first need to create or obtain the type of ticket to label the new ticket. Then you can create the ticket using a curl request or with a programming language of your choice. [Follow this guide](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/tickets/create-a-ticket/) from our developer documentation to create a ticket type and create a new ticket. ## How can I flag back office tickets so they aren't counted when using the API? If you are using the API to retrieve tickets and ticket data, you can use the[ search tickets API endpoint](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Tickets/searchTickets/). To exclude back office ticket types, set the field to `ticket_type_id` and use the `!=` operator to exclude the `ticket_type_id` assigned to back office ticket types. If you are using the API to [retrieve a conversation](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Conversations/retrieveConversation/) or [list conversations](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Conversations/listConversations/) with back office tickets associated with the conversations and you'd like to exclude them, you can similarly filter out any results that have the back office ticket type as an attribute. Linked tickets can be found at the tickets parameter in the response or under linked_objects. One other option available is to [use the API to tag conversations](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Tags/attachTagToConversation/) with a back office ticket associated with them. You can then use the tag in order to filter by ticket category. # Error Codes and Messages ## What does a 403 API Plan restricted error message in a response mean? If you are getting a 403 API Plan restricted message in a response this means that the API you are trying to use is not available on your app's plan. In order to access the API you'll need to upgrade your plan. You can find out more about Intercom plans[ on this page](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/8420845-intercom-plans-explained). You can find a full list of[ error codes](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/errors/error-codes/) and[ HTTP responses](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/errors/http-responses/) in our developer documentation. ## What does a 409 conflict error message in a response mean? If you are getting a 409 conflict message in a response this means there is existing data in your Intercom workspace that clashes with the request data. This can occur if you try to[ create a contact](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Contacts/CreateContact/) and there is a contact with that email address already added within your app. To avoid this error you can use the update endpoint instead or create a new contact by external_id. You can find a full list of[ error codes](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/errors/error-codes/) and[ HTTP responses](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/errors/http-responses/) in our developer documentation. ## What does a 429 error message in a response mean? ## What are the current rate limits? Private apps have a default rate limit of 10,000 API calls per minute per workspace, shared by all private apps in the workspace. This means that if a workspace has multiple private apps installed, every one contributes towards the same total. Public apps have a default rate limit of 10,000 API calls per minute for each app and 25,000 API calls per minute per workspace. This means that if a workspace has multiple public apps installed, each one has its own separate request limit without contributing to the others. More information on rate limits is available in our [developer documentation](https://developers.intercom.com/docs). # Reporting ## Why is my report different when pulled from the API vs UI? If you are creating your own reports using the API you may notice that there are some differences between the two reports. This can happen for a few reasons. One common issue is when dates and times do not match. This is often because the time zone that you are using in your Intercom workspace is different than the time zone you are using to query the API. To fix this, either adjust your API query parameters to match your workspace time zone, or change the time zone of your custom report. Another issue is that you may be using metrics that do not align with the Intercom reporting UI metrics. There are some metrics available in the reporting UI that are not available via the API because they are calculated metrics. Some of those can be created by using the API and performing the calculations on your end. Check out the[ guide for building your own reports](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/rest-apis/build-your-own-reports/) from the Intercom developer documentation. ## Are back office tickets counted in the statistics when pulling a report from API? If you are looking at the conversations reports available in the UI versus reports pulled using the conversations API, you may notice that there is a difference in the number of conversations. This is because back office tickets associated with a conversation will be included when it is pulled from the API. To solve for this, you can filter results after retrieving them via the[ list conversations](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/preview/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Conversations/listConversations/),[ retrieve a conversation](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/preview/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Conversations/retrieveConversation/), or[ search for conversations](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/preview/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Conversations/searchConversations/) API, and separate the tickets from conversations using the ticket field in the conversation API response. The ticket field will be populated with an object if it is a ticket and will be null if it is a conversation. # Webhooks ## What webhooks are available? Webhooks allow you to subscribe to real-time notifications of events happening in Intercom, like when a contact is created or an incoming message is received. ## Are there plans to add new webhooks? There are no plans to add new webhooks on our roadmap, but if there is a webhook your team needs, please submit a request to the team or add it to the[ product wishlist](https://community.intercom.com/ideas) in the Intercom community. ## Webhook reliability and delivery When building on Intercom webhooks, keep the following in mind: - **Retry policy:** Intercom retries failed webhook deliveries. If your endpoint returns a non-2xx response, Intercom will retry the request. Design your endpoint to handle duplicate deliveries (make it idempotent). - **Timeout:** Your endpoint must respond within a short window. If it times out, the delivery is treated as a failure and retried. - **Ordering:** Webhook events are not guaranteed to arrive in the exact order they occurred. Use event timestamps to sequence events correctly in your system. - **Debugging:** The Developer Hub doesn't show a history of webhook deliveries or the payloads that were sent. To debug missed or malformed events, log incoming requests on your own endpoint, including the topic, notification ID and response code you return. In the Developer Hub, under your app's webhook settings, you can preview an example payload for each topic, and saving your webhook settings sends a test request to your endpoint URL to confirm it can receive notifications. If you need help investigating specific deliveries, contact Fin Support. # Pagination ## How does pagination work? Intercom APIs for[ listing](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/rest-apis/pagination/#pagination-for-list-apis) and[ searching](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/rest-apis/pagination/#pagination-for-search-apis) resources offer cursor-based pagination. This is available so that when you are requesting a large amount of data — like many conversations with all of their parts — you can receive and process them in smaller chunks. For examples on how to use pagination with both the Intercom list APIs, which accept path parameters, and search APIs, which use query parameters, see our[ pagination guide](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/rest-apis/pagination/). ## How do I used the starting_after field? For cursor-based pagination, Intercom uses a pointer that will refer to a specific record based on the limit that you set by the number of pages that you specify per request. When returned in an object, the pointer will look something like 'WzXXXXXXXXXXXXXX'. You can then use the pointer from the response in order to make the subsequent request for the next batch of data. The pagination formatting in the request differs slightly between list APIs and search APIs, but the responses work the same. # Authentication ## What type of authentication is required for public apps? Any apps that interact with third party workspace data and apps built with Canvas Kit require OAuth to be in place. You should never ask users for their access token and only use OAuth for interacting with their data. ## Do I have to use OAuth for my app? You'll need to set up OAuth if you're building an integration with Intercom that accesses other peoples' Intercom data. This includes public apps that you plan to list on the Intercom app store as well as apps and integrations you will ask users to install through your own website. Learn more about OAuth from[ our developer documentation](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication/#oauth). If you are only accessing data within you own Intercom workspace you can use an[ access token](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication/#access-tokens). ## What type of authentication is required for private apps? If you're building a private app that only accesses data in your Intercom workspace, you can use your Intercom access token for authentication. Find your access token in your developer hub and[ learn more about authentication here](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication/). ## Where can I find my Intercom access token? You can use your Intercom access token if you're using the API to access data in your own Intercom workspace. Find your access token in your developer hub and[ learn more about authentication here](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication/). To find your API access token, follow these steps: 1. Open the **Intercom Developer Hub**. 2. Navigate to **Your Apps** at Developer Hub > Settings > Your Apps. You should see a list of apps associated with your workspace. 3. Locate your private app, which may include your workspace’s name and sometimes the suffix "Access Token App." 4. Click the app name to open its details. 5. Go to the **Authentication** section to find the token. Treat this token like a password, as it is private and should not be shared. ## Can I rotate or change my OAuth Client Secret? You can't rotate your app's OAuth Client Secret yourself, but our support team can rotate it for you on request. Once it's rotated, the old secret stops working immediately and the new secret is available in the Developer Hub. **Important:** The old secret is invalidated immediately upon rotation. Be ready to update your integration's configuration as soon as the rotation takes place to avoid any service interruption. To request a rotation, message us in the Messenger and ask to speak to the support team. Include your app's name and Client ID, and agree on a time for the rotation so your team can update your integration's configuration with the new secret straight away. # Installing and Publishing Apps ## How do I build an app for my Inbox? You can build an app for your Intercom Inbox by using Canvas Kit, a toolkit that allows you to build apps that work from directly within the Intercom UI. ## How do I build an app for my Messenger? You can build an app for your Intercom Messenger by using Canvas Kit, a toolkit that allows you to build apps that work from directly within the Intercom UI. Note that customizations are limited to what is capable through Canvas Kit and must be created within the Messenger: it's not possible to recreate or re-skin the Messenger. ## How do I install my app? If you visit the Test & Publish > Your Workspaces page of your app in the [Developer Hub](https://app.intercom.com/a/apps/_/developer-hub) then you should see all the workspaces you (as an Intercom teammate) are a member of. You can click on Install app next to the workspace you want to install the given app on. This app will then be installed and an[ Access Token](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication/#access-tokens) will be provided for that workspace so you can access its data through the API. ## How can I publish my app to the Intercom app store? When you are ready to publish your app, you can follow the steps in the developer hub. You can find a guide on how to publish your app in [our developer documentation](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/publish-to-the-app-store/review-publish-your-app/). # Messenger ## How do I install the Messenger for iOS? The Intercom SDK (Software Development Kit) for iOS enables you to use the [Intercom Messenger](https://www.intercom.com/messenger) in your app, have conversations with your customers, send rich outbound messages, show your Help Center, and track events. You can install Intercom for iOS using Cocoapods, Swift Package Manager, or manually. Read the full [iOS installation guide](https://developers.intercom.com/installing-intercom/ios/installation/). You can find Intercom for iOS [on GitHub](https://github.com/intercom/intercom-ios/) along with a [sample app](https://github.com/intercom/intercom-ios/tree/master/Examples) to explore the SDK. ## How do I install the Messenger for Android? The Intercom SDK for Android enables you to use the [Intercom Messenger](https://www.intercom.com/messenger) in your app, have conversations with your customers, send rich outbound messages, show your Help Center, and track events. ## How do I install the Messenger for React Native? --- 💡**Tip** **Need more help?** Get support from our [Community Forum](https://community.intercom.com/?utm_source=ii-help-center&utm_medium=internal) Find answers and get help from Intercom Support and Community Experts ---
